requirement: Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page, and each rendered requirement and example MUST be followed by a "See evidence" link to that page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and, when an index exists, to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Every obligation in `requirements.index.navigation` has code that carries it out and a test that asserts the outcome. I judged this from the supplied source items and did not read further source. | Obligation | Code | Test | |---|---|---| | Each requirement and example definition badge links to its detail page. | `replace_definitions` in `src/lib.rs` emits an `` badge when a detail plan exists, and `chapter_href` builds the relative link. | `every_definition_gets_a_nested_detail_page_without_an_index` asserts `id="habeas-req-…" href="…"` for two requirements and one example. The index test asserts the same for `requirements.core.ready`. | | Each rendered requirement and example is followed by a "See evidence" link to that page. | `replace_definitions` appends `

The `anchor` function in `src/lib.rs` matches the `id` that `replace_definitions` emits. | `every_definition_gets_a_nested_detail_page_without_an_index` and the index test assert `[View definition](../rules.html#habeas-req-rules.zeta)` and `[View definition](../core.html#habeas-req-requirements.core.ready)`. | | When an index exists, each detail page links to the index. | `render_detail_page` prepends `[Requirements index](index_href) · ` only when `index_path` is `Some`. `populate` passes `self.index_path`. | The index test asserts `[Requirements index](../../appendix/requirements-index.html) · [View definition]`. The no-index test asserts that "Requirements index" is absent. | | Reference badges continue to link to the definition. | `reference_badge` builds an ``. `replace_inline_references` uses it. | `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` asserts the `impl`, `cite` and `test` badge hrefs. | | Links resolve when a name contains `.md`. | `chapter_href` replaces `.md` with `%2Emd`. | `links_preserve_requirement_names_containing_md` checks both link directions. The no-index test also covers `rules.cli.mdbook` for the badge, "See evidence" and back-link. | The example detail page's back-link goes through the same code as the requirement one, with no separate branch, so it needs no separate test. I saw no unspecified behavior. The other generated output, such as index table rows and source paths, is covered by other requirements that the same items mark with `{impl}`.
